title: Mathematicians open a public edit of OpenAI's math write-ups
friendlyTitle: Mathematicians have opened a public edit of OpenAI's math notes
summary: Terence Tao has posted a guest note from Abhinav Nellore, Johannes Schmitt, Soledad Villar, and Rachel Ward. They say OpenAI's math write-ups, published at github.com/openai/math, can be hard to follow and can cite incompletely. They have opened github.com/mathcommunity/oai-math-revised as a place for students, postdocs, professors, and other readers to revise those notes. A browsable copy is at mathcommunity.github.io/oai-math-revised. They are also asking for volunteer reviewers by topic.
friendlySummary: Terence Tao has posted a guest note from Abhinav Nellore, Johannes Schmitt, Soledad Villar, and Rachel Ward. They say OpenAI's math write-ups, at github.com/openai/math, can be hard to follow and can leave citations incomplete. They have opened github.com/mathcommunity/oai-math-revised so students, researchers, and other readers can revise those notes. A readable copy is at mathcommunity.github.io/oai-math-revised. They are also asking for volunteer reviewers by topic.
whyItMatters: If you are using an AI lab's math post as evidence that a model solved something, the write-up is part of the claim. A public revision log is a way to see which steps were unclear, which citations were missing, and which corrections the community actually made. It does not settle whether the model did the work. It does make the paper trail readable by someone who was not in the room.
